newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on export, crusher buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on export, crusher buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended higher on export and crusher demand but off the day's highs under pressure from a flagging CBOT soycomplex, traders said.

"Crushers bought 1,000 November and there's talk of a canola oil sale to the U.S. Chicago's sell-off late in the day brought canola $1 off the top at the close and the pools had MOC hedges," a trader said. Volume was heavy at 6,044 lots, or 120,880 tonnes, with 1,150 hedge lots. Jan-Mar spread $1.10, Nov-Jan $4.20, Sep-Nov at $2.50 and Nov-Mar $5.50.
Japan bought 15,000-20,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
November canola rose $2.80 to $436.40, January up $2.30 to $440.30. November flax up $1 to $371.50 after triggering buy stops at $374. Hedges weighed on flax late in the day.

October feed wheat lost $0.40 to $202.50 on talk rain and some frost in Alberta will produce more feed wheat. December closed up $0.40 at $185.90. Oct-Mar spread at $18.50, Dec-Mar $4, Mar-May $1. Volume was 940 lots.

November western barley rose $1.30 to $148.30 and February was up $1 at $152.70 on Alberta Wheat Pool short covering and feedlot buying, traders said. Nov-Feb spread at $4.50. Oct-Dec peas spread at US$2.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
